findings.text: follow-on: the integrated-gate landing calls _commit_landing_writes and discards the returned landing_check, so a staged reversal or a post-commit mismatch found while landing the gate re-run is appended to landing.json and read by nobody — the same gap the repair closed for the release site at promotion_release.py:636, still present at the third call site; the file lies outside this node's declared write paths so it was fenced from repair, and it is the module's own claim that every landing sites through _report_landing_check which this call site falsifies.

follow-on: test_logs and negative_control_note (line 19) both cite /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261018T213033460177-a-landing-checks-what-it-left/negative-control-repair.log, which does not exist on disk (only negative-control-base.log is present), so the repair-arm negative control that validates the second review finding's fix is a pointer no reader can open.

follow-on: `assert recorded["worktree_released"] is True` compares the value _record_release_on_ledger returned against the very dict the test passed in as release={'worktree_released': True}, so the two sides move together and the assertion holds whether or not anything was persisted; the no-change property this case guards is carried instead by the independent read at line 224 (persisted = json.loads(run_file.read_text()) checked against a literal) and the head equality at line 228, so the weak assertion does not by itself guard the refusal it names.
